builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Stochastic Motion Tokenization
summary: The method replaces velocity-commanded RL interfaces and reference-blind tracking policies with discrete stochastic motion tokens generated by a high-level controller that condition a whole-body tracking policy. Adoption requires training a motion tokenizer and RL tracking policies plus access to a physical humanoid (Unitree G1) and motion data; sim-to-real transfer and tokenizer reconstruction quality are the main costs in engineering effort. It can fail when generated token sequences request motions outside the tracking policy's training distribution, during behavior transitions the tokenizer represents poorly, or when reconstruction errors produce dynamically infeasible references on hardware.
rationale: This is a robotics whole-body control method requiring a physical humanoid platform, and it offers no applicable technique for an AI/ML engineer focused on production LLM or model-serving work on a single 24 GB GPU.
technique: Stochastic motion tokenization for humanoid tracking control

claims.statement: The method replaces velocity-commanded RL interfaces and reference-blind tracking policies with discrete stochastic motion tokens generated by a high-level controller that condition a whole-body tracking policy. Adoption requires training a motion tokenizer and RL tracking policies plus access to a physical humanoid (Unitree G1) and motion data; sim-to-real transfer and tokenizer reconstruction quality are the main costs in engineering effort. It can fail when generated token sequences request motions outside the tracking policy's training distribution, during behavior transitions the tokenizer represents poorly, or when reconstruction errors produce dynamically infeasible references on hardware.

At matched capacity, the stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs Unitree G1 motions better than FSQ and VQ-VAE baselines (no numeric factor given); policies execute 16.8 s dance/fight/walk motions and a 35 s fight-to-dance sequence on a physical G1.
